title: Form Validation
description: Learn how to validate form inputs and display error messages.

data.text: Form validation ensures users enter correct data before submission. React makes it easy to validate inputs and provide immediate feedback by storing errors in state and conditionally rendering messages.
You can validate on every keystroke, when the user leaves a field (on blur), or only when the form is submitted. For the best user experience, combine real-time and submit-time validation.

data.title: When to Validate
items: **On change** — instant feedback, but can be annoying if too aggressive.
**On blur** — validates when the user leaves the field; a great middle ground.
**On submit** — catches all errors at once; required as a safety net.

data.text: Store the error message in state alongside the value. Clear the error once the input becomes valid.

data.title: Email Validation

data.text: For forms with many fields, keep errors in an object where each key matches a field name.

data.title: Registration Validation

data.text: Validate when the user leaves a field rather than on every keystroke. This avoids frustration while still providing timely feedback.

data.title: Blur Validation
data.content: Validating when the user leaves a field

data.title: Accessibility Matters
data.text: Use aria-invalid and role="alert" for error messages so screen readers announce them. Always link labels to inputs with htmlFor and id.

terms.definition: Checking that user input meets defined rules before processing.
Validating when the user leaves a field, balancing feedback speed with annoyance.
A state object that maps field names to error messages.

data.title: Exercise: Validate a Contact Form
data.description: Add validation to a contact form with name, email, and message fields.
steps: Create a ContactForm component with three controlled inputs.
Validate that name is not empty, email matches a regex, and message is at least 10 characters.
Show errors on blur and on submit.
Disable the submit button when errors exist.
data.expectedOutcome: A contact form that prevents invalid submissions and guides the user with clear error messages.

items.question: Should I validate on the client, server, or both?
items.answer: Always both. Client validation improves UX, but server validation is mandatory for security because client code can be bypassed.

items.question: Can I use a regex for all validation?
items.answer: Regex is great for format checks (email, phone). For business rules (password strength, uniqueness), combine regex with custom logic.

items.question: What is debouncing in validation?
items.answer: Delaying validation slightly after the user stops typing to avoid excessive re-renders and annoying feedback.

items.question: Should I use a form library?
items.answer: For simple forms, manual validation is fine. For complex forms with many fields, consider React Hook Form or Formik for built-in validation and performance.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Validate on change, blur, and submit for the best UX.
Store errors in state and render them conditionally.
Use accessible markup: labels, htmlFor, aria-invalid, role=alert.
Client validation is for UX; server validation is for security.
data.takeaway: Good validation catches errors early and guides users toward correct input. Next, you'll learn how to submit the form data to a server.
